title: Artin--Schreier model of characteristic-p degree-one pullback
statement: Let f:C→Spec(k) be a smooth proper connected curve of dimension at most one [def-sc-curves, def-weil-proper-morphism], k⊆k′ algebraically closed fields of characteristic p>0, and C′ its base change. For every commutative coefficient ring Λ, the H¹ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] pullback for the constant sheaf Λ/(p) admits compatible additive equivalences with I→₀V^F and I→₀(k′⊗_kV)^{F′}, where V is a finite-dimensional k-vector space, F is p-semilinear, F′ is its tensor extension, and pullback in every coordinate is v↦1⊗v. This is a model and compatibility assertion, without asserting that the map of fixed points is bijective.

source.place: proof, Artin--Schreier kernels and flat coherent base change; Tags 02KH, 03Q5, 0739 for flat base change and coefficient colimits

proof.text: Use the Artin--Schreier sequence and proper degree-zero surjectivity to identify H¹(C,Z/p) with the fixed subgroup of Frobenius on the finite-dimensional coherent H¹(C,O_C). The Ext/derived comparison transfers the sequence to the cohomology convention in the statement. In dimension zero both degree-one groups vanish.

Apply flat coherent base change (Stacks 02KH) to H¹(O_C). Functoriality of powers identifies the pulled-back Frobenius with its semilinear tensor extension F′ and gives F′(1 tensor v)=1 tensor F(v). Naturality of Artin--Schreier identifies the map on the two kernels. This step constructs and identifies the comparison; it does not prove that the fixed-point map is bijective.

Choose a prime-field basis of Λ/(p). The finite-sum colimit presentation and large-universe cohomology continuity identify H¹ of its constant sheaf with finitely supported families of H¹(C,Z/p). Apply the same presentation after inverse image; naturality yields the displayed coordinate identity. The empty basis handles Λ/(p)=0.
